hemomancy.artificer.item_inquiry.monolit.about: the Artificer describing Monolith Imbued Cloth as soft but taught to carry weight that ordinary cloth was never meant to remember
the Artificer saying the Monolith Imbued Cloth is used in Silent Archon vestment work once the frame has taken the Cornerstone

hemomancy.circus.captive.severed.about: a system message that the captive's thread has snapped, that the named captive (the captive's name) dies with it, and that the anchor beneath the carousel horse is now exposed

hemomancy.circus.challenge.begin.0.about: a challenge-start message telling the player to begin by keeping the trained peacock spider in sight until its dance ends, and that it will not attack

hemomancy.circus.challenge.begin.2.about: a challenge-start message telling the player to begin by staying inside the ring and withstanding the dolls until the act ends

hemomancy.circus.challenge.begin.3.about: a challenge-start message telling the player to begin by watching the Knife Thrower, because the blade flies straight but the setup is crooked

hemomancy.circus.challenge.begin.4.about: a challenge-start message telling the player to begin by staying in the ring until the troupe finishes the carousel pattern

hemomancy.circus.challenge.complete.0.about: a challenge completion message confirming the player having kept the spider in sight until the dance ended

hemomancy.circus.challenge.complete.2.about: a challenge completion message confirming the player having held the ring until the dolls stopped

hemomancy.circus.challenge.complete.3.about: a challenge completion message confirming the player having read the Knife Thrower's rhythm and survived the act

hemomancy.circus.challenge.complete.4.about: a challenge completion message confirming the player having held the ring until the carousel pattern ended

hemomancy.circus.challenge.failed.about: a message that the act is over and the player should speak to the Ringmaster when ready to try again

hemomancy.circus.challenge.hold.0.about: a mid-act reminder that the spider is still dancing and the player must keep their eyes on it

hemomancy.circus.challenge.hold.2.about: a mid-act reminder that the dolls are committed and the player must hold their ground

hemomancy.circus.challenge.hold.3.about: a mid-act reminder that the player has found the thrower's rhythm and must not lose it

hemomancy.circus.challenge.hold.4.about: a mid-act reminder that the troupe is halfway through the pattern and the player must stay in the ring

hemomancy.circus.discovery.about: a discovery message that the rough pavilion comes into focus and the player has found the Circus

hemomancy.circus.finale.claimed.about: a message that another performer has already claimed this pavilion and it will not answer the player

hemomancy.circus.finale.complete.liberat.about: narration of the Liberation finale ending: the Ringmaster falls, the three captives and their anchors are gone, and the carousel is ruined for good

hemomancy.circus.finale.complete.success.about: narration of the Succession finale ending: the Ringmaster yields and lives, his office becomes a pattern, and the pavilion stays standing

hemomancy.circus.finale.empty_troupe.about: narration that no troupe members are left to fall, so the ring stands empty and the Ringmaster comes down to face the player himself

hemomancy.circus.finale.not_ready.about: a message that the player is not ready for Succession and must finish every controlled act and complete their attunement first

hemomancy.circus.finale.ringmaster_lost.about: a message that the Ringmaster vanished before the finale ended, so the pavilion releases the player and the act closes unfinished

hemomancy.circus.option.accept.about: accepting the Ringmaster's bargain by saying they will succeed him

hemomancy.circus.option.confirm_liberati.about: confirming Liberation, saying they know the cost and will end the pavilion

hemomancy.circus.option.confirm_successi.about: confirming Succession, saying they understand and asking to be bound to it

hemomancy.circus.option.not_yet.about: declining for now by saying not yet

hemomancy.circus.option.reject.about: rejecting the Ringmaster's offer and vowing to break the carousel and free its captives

hemomancy.circus.option.repair.about: saying they chose wrong and asking to use their one chance to change their route

hemomancy.circus.option.trial.about: asking the Ringmaster to show them the next act

hemomancy.circus.ringmaster.line.liberat.about: the Ringmaster explaining that three failed initiates ride the carousel, that cutting their threads kills their bodies but not the anchors beneath them, and that the player must break the anchors too
the Ringmaster's closing line after Liberation, saying only the ruin answers the player now

hemomancy.circus.ringmaster.line.neutral.about: the Ringmaster laying out the bargain: take his place, cut the others free, or walk out of the tent

hemomancy.circus.ringmaster.line.success.about: the Ringmaster telling the player to learn every act and hold every eye in the pavilion, then come take his hat and the office bound to it
the Ringmaster's closing line after Succession, saying the pavilion knows its successor and answers to the player

hemomancy.circus.ringmaster.silent.about: narration of the figure in the rafters looking through the player and refusing to take shape for them yet

hemomancy.circus.ringmaster.warning.libe.about: a warning that choosing Liberation kills the three bound initiates when their threads are severed, then the player breaks the carousel and leaves the pavilion in ruins, with one change of mind allowed only before either ending is complete

hemomancy.circus.ringmaster.warning.succ.about: a warning that choosing Succession keeps the pavilion standing but binds its trials to the player, with one chance to change their mind before either ending completes

hemomancy.circus.school.aftermath.libera.about: a professor noting that the player chose Liberation, and that cutting the captive strings kills the people bound to them, so no living prisoners will walk free
a professor saying the captives and Ringmaster are dead and the carousel ruined, that teaching continues from the surviving camps, and that no victory brings those people back

hemomancy.circus.school.aftermath.neutra.about: a professor saying nobody has settled the Ringmaster's bargain yet and the player may take lessons without agreeing to either ending

hemomancy.circus.school.aftermath.succes.about: a professor noting the player chose Succession, that its final act is the Ringmaster's usual challenges, and that the apprenticeship adds nothing to it
a professor noting that Succession left the pavilion standing and gave the player its Pattern, and that professors keep teaching even those who distrust the bargain

hemomancy.circus.school.ask_aftermath.about: asking a professor what happens to the school after the final act

hemomancy.circus.school.ask_colleagues.about: asking a professor what they think of the other professors

hemomancy.circus.school.ask_history.about: asking a professor how they joined the Troupe

hemomancy.circus.school.ask_preparation.about: asking a professor what the player should prepare

hemomancy.circus.school.back.about: returning to the earlier conversation with the professor

hemomancy.circus.school.circus_acrobat.a.about: the Acrobat promising the ropes will stay sound for the next pupil, and saying whoever conducts next does not get to tell the wings how to remember flight

hemomancy.circus.school.circus_acrobat.c.about: the Acrobat describing their act as up, strike, back down, noting pupils forget the down while the Fire Breather does not since an act needs a recovery as much as an entrance, and that the Strongman calls it a wasted lift, which they dismiss

hemomancy.circus.school.circus_acrobat.h.about: the Acrobat explaining they came to rigging first and blood after, then fell when a line snapped without choosing it, and that climbing down means choosing every hand, a difference their Vultures keep in their wing joints

hemomancy.circus.school.circus_acrobat.l.about: the Acrobat pointing out the Veinwing Vulture's wing spars and scarlet tendons, explaining it is built never hatched as an aerial striker, requiring Degree 3, preparing its frame and its Cardinal Ordeal, then a practical where it chases a rehearsal threat from the air, hits it, and swings back when recalled

hemomancy.circus.school.circus_acrobat.t.about: the Acrobat testifying from the rigging that an understudy climbed down from the loft and then had no name in the next program, and that the wrong audience watched the performers' hands the whole time, never the act

hemomancy.circus.school.circus_acrobat.w.about: the Acrobat greeting a player whose Vulture hovers at their shoulder, saying it catches nothing on its own, so the player must give it a line to chase and then a reason to swing back

hemomancy.circus.school.circus_beast_tam.about: the Beast Tamer saying that, like geese, the pack finds its way without a pavilion, and that when this site is done the other camps go on teaching

the Beast Tamer comparing a startled flock scattering to their pack, noting the Stilt Walker's opposite trick of pinning every eye to one spot, and saying the Fire Breather's worry about singeing a Cur is exactly why they trust that professor's lessons

the Beast Tamer explaining they came in with a cage and learned to leave it empty, that a living animal has its own needs unlike a built Hound bound to a Crossbar, and that the Court's living creatures deserve better than how the stage talks about them

the Beast Tamer teaching that a Hound is a pack waiting to happen: at Degree 4 prepare the Sanguine Hound bridle and take its Cardinal Ordeal, then in the practical let rehearsal threats wound the Hound until it ruptures and get one temporary Blood Cur to land a hit, with the warning that a Cur cannot be learned, called separately or kept as another permanent shape

the Beast Tamer testifying that as someone who counts mouths they noticed three names dropped from the traveling roster while their rations kept appearing on the pavilion account, and telling the player to read the tally copied in the loft as more honest than any stage farewell

the Beast Tamer saying a pack changes shape when one of its own goes down, as with a Hound's rupture, so the player should handle the body gently and, once it bursts, let its temporary Curs finish the chase

hemomancy.circus.school.circus_fire_eate.about: the Fire Breather giving two outcomes after the final act: the troupe can perform among ruins without setting them alight, and the surviving camps can be where pupils learn control again

the Fire Breather naming two colleagues and two rules, the Beast Tamer's account for every allied body in the ring and the Strongman's wind-up the back row can see, and saying both hold because a dangerous act ought to announce itself

the Fire Breather explaining that the oldest frame handed to them stood on brittle legs, so they gave it a serpent's lower body so the gaunt upper half could spend its effort on the lungs, then left the ribs open so a pupil can read the pressure before the mouth opens

the Fire Breather teaching at Degree 4: build a Cinder Bellows Frame from hematic iron scraps, leather, Filaments and blaze powder; the ordeal is a Dominion Lesser at 900 mL that consumes the frame only once the Bellows manifests, so the Crossbar survives; then count one second inhale, two seconds a five-block sixty-degree cone, two seconds recover; the practical is hitting both rehearsal threats in one breath, and it never breathes through walls or onto allies or sets terrain alight

the Fire Breather giving an ordered account: first the three understudies rehearsing ordinary entrances, later the Ringmaster calling their absence a change in casting, and between the two they never saw the understudies leave the grounds
the Fire Breather stating the order of their craft: the serpent coil steadies the body first, the lung-sac steadies the breath next, and fire comes third, never first

hemomancy.circus.school.circus_knife_thr.about: the Dagger Thrower saying that if the pavilion stands they teach in its blade ring, if it falls a wagon floor will do, and either way the Ringmaster will not own the next generation of hands

the Dagger Thrower dismissing the Stilt Walker's claim that a distracted enemy is beaten, arguing distraction only buys time for a deliberate throw, and admitting neither will win the argument because both have seen a careless pupil hurt the audience

the Dagger Thrower admitting they once threw one knife, hit, and thought themselves a genius, then the Juggler taught them the empty hands between throws matter too, shown by a laughing mask, a grieving one and a blank one on the same suspended frame

the Dagger Thrower explaining the Marrow Juggler is the old Marrow Spitter renamed with the same ordeal and Crossbar, requiring Degree 3, preparing its offering and unlocking it, then commanding a full three-dagger volley into one rehearsal threat, and correcting that the three throws split one attack's strength rather than tripling damage

the Dagger Thrower testifying that the wrong audience applauded a puppet's bow but ignored a performer because they wanted obedience not craft, then telling the player to get the Stilt Walker's side too and prove they can focus without giving up control
the Dagger Thrower saying six hands are worthless until they agree on one target, only in theory, and that their Juggler wears three faces to show how often the theory loses

hemomancy.circus.school.circus_stilt_wal.about: the Stilt Walker saying a mask can go on looking after a pupil even when the conductor has lost their stage, but refusing to call a dead captive a liberated student

the Stilt Walker arguing that several imperfect targets all looking away from a pupil protect better than one perfect target, noting the Dagger Thrower will dispute it and the Beast Tamer would split the pack, while they prefer every eye in the ring turned the same way
the Stilt Walker explaining that from over the crowd they could see who watched the show and who looked for the exit, and built the Mummer so the frightened ones would have somewhere else to look

the Stilt Walker teaching at the fourth Degree: learn the Scarlet Mummer, complete its Cardinal Ordeal, bring your own known body, then in the practical two rehearsal threats chase the player or an allied puppet and the Mummer must draw both away using only its pulse and one evasive step

the Stilt Walker testifying that the wrong audience could not tell an act from a command and the understudies had stopped choosing their own entrances well before they vanished, pointing the player to the Dagger Thrower who was down among them, then asking the player to show attention spent protecting somebody
the Stilt Walker explaining the Scarlet Mummer borrows an enemy's attention for a little while so the player can hold it long enough for somebody else to breathe

hemomancy.circus.school.circus_strongman.about: the Strongman saying they can rebuild a practice ring but not the people under that carousel, and that forgetting them leaves the player practicing alone
the Strongman contrasting the Acrobat who knows when to leave with themselves who know where to stay, and saying a conductor who cannot value both breaks every string they own

the Strongman recalling that their first body lifted a wagon but could not hold a door for one scared child, strong and good for nothing, and that this one wears belt and tendon bindings whose burden the player can see

the Strongman teaching at Fourth Degree: prepare the Gorebound Hulk offering and beat its Cardinal Ordeal, then in the practical Anchor Guard inside the ring, keep the Hulk guarding for five seconds and make it hit a rehearsal threat while still guarding, describing its small head, lifting belt and heavy forearms as built like a strongman

the Strongman recalling being told the understudies were on a traveling engagement while their luggage stayed under the beds, challenging the player to repeat that lie and telling them to go look at those rooms
the Strongman saying the Hulk's shoulders make a promise to plant where trouble lands and that it keeps its word, then asking the player whether they do

hemomancy.circus.school.circus_threadkee.about: the Threadkeeper saying the scattered camps teach as much as the pavilion, and that the player's finished work and any guest pay still owed stay on their account, not the building's

the Threadkeeper explaining two promises are on the books, the Ringmaster's grand final act and the faculty's promise of a pupil who can call one body, control it and dismiss it safely, and that they can inspect only the second so they start there
the Threadkeeper explaining they once counted ticket money and now the book holds Crossbar charge, spare Filaments and returning pupils' reports, and that a good account tells you what is still owed

the Threadkeeper opening the account entry An Empty Ring: hold up an attuned, charged Crossbar for inspection, learn any shape and complete its ordeal, call, command and recall with that same Crossbar and report back, noting each professor records their own practical and story investigations and paid guest performances go in the Side ledger

the Threadkeeper listing two open items: the wrong audience closes on the Stilt Walker's and Dagger Thrower's accounts with both practicals passed, and the missing understudy closes on the abandoned stage record, loft account, quarters letter, carousel tally and the Retired Understudy's testimony, promising to close both when given the facts
the Threadkeeper asking for the player's own instrument so they can check the binding and enter it, noting the professors teach what goes on its strings

hemomancy.circus.school.circus_understud.about: the Retired Understudy insisting the missing performers were people and that whatever is left of the school keeps their names on the bill, whether a successor takes the Pattern or the carousel ends in blood

the Retired Understudy saying memory bends easily so they are glad the Threadkeeper keeps accounts, that they do not much mind a blank face on the Juggler, but are troubled by a conductor who claims every remembered face as their own like a lead taking the whole company's bows

the Retired Understudy explaining an understudy learns another performer's pauses, flubs and ways out of them, and that they had retired by the time the Ringmaster decided a perfect replacement should never need a choice of its own

the Retired Understudy teaching that the player needs the fifth Degree and the Mnemonist Puppet's ordeal done first, then in the practical must strike a rehearsal threat while the known puppet watches, keeping the threat in its range until it replays the recorded attack, and apologizing that ordinary puppet melee will not count as an echo

the Retired Understudy identifying the three entries as the missing understudies whose cues they knew, insisting nobody left those beds to tour, saying the stage program, loft account and quarters tell one story and the carousel tally tells the ending: they are what the Ringmaster made of them

the Retired Understudy explaining that a Mnemonist body repeats an attack it has watched, as they once learned a lead's business from the wings, so the player should give it a real memory first and then listen for the echo

hemomancy.circus.school.claim.about: asking to collect their remaining Filaments

hemomancy.circus.school.clue.carousel.about: a ledger clue that the carousel tally confirms the three missing performers are its bound captives, that severing the strings is lethal, and that the player should bring this evidence and the Retired Understudy's testimony to a Threadkeeper

hemomancy.circus.school.clue.loft.about: a ledger clue that the rigging account records three substitutions with the same names copied into the carousel's passenger tally, a margin note says their rooms were never reassigned, and the player should search the understudy quarters

hemomancy.circus.school.clue.quarters.about: a ledger clue that three unused beds and an unfinished letter contradict the announcement that the understudies left on tour, that the Retired Understudy can identify them, and that the player should examine the carousel tally itself

hemomancy.circus.school.clue.stage.about: a ledger clue that a torn program names an understudy in the role of a living person with a penciled correction to carousel support, and the player should find the rigging account in the pavilion loft

hemomancy.circus.school.conductor.about: asking about the school and its conductor

hemomancy.circus.school.exercise.gorebou.about: an exercise card describing the Gorebound Hulk practical: holding Guard in the ring for five seconds and landing a guarded strike, using the player's own known body and Crossbar, staying near the professor

hemomancy.circus.school.exercise.marrow_.about: an exercise card describing the Marrow Juggler practical: landing all three daggers of one volley on one rehearsal threat, using the player's own known body and Crossbar, staying near the professor

hemomancy.circus.school.exercise.mnemoni.about: an exercise card describing the Mnemonist Puppet practical: striking a threat personally and then having the puppet replay that observed attack, using the player's own known body and Crossbar, staying near the professor

hemomancy.circus.school.exercise.sanguin.about: an exercise card describing the Sanguine Hound practical: letting the Hound rupture and then hitting a rehearsal threat with its temporary Curs, using the player's own known body and Crossbar, staying near the professor

hemomancy.circus.school.exercise.scarlet.about: an exercise card describing the Scarlet Mummer practical: diverting both rehearsal threats away from the player or an allied puppet, using the player's own known body and Crossbar, staying near the professor

hemomancy.circus.school.exercise.veinwin.about: an exercise card describing the Veinwing Vulture practical: pursuing from the air, hitting a rehearsal threat, then recalling the body, using the player's own known body and Crossbar, staying near the professor

a ledger step telling the player to report both accounts and practicals to a Threadkeeper at Degree 4
a ledger step telling the player to hear the Stilt Walker's and the Dagger Thrower's accounts

hemomancy.circus.school.not_ready.about: a professor saying the player needs active blood and the Degree the shape calls for before instruction can begin, and that nothing has been recorded

hemomancy.circus.school.passed.about: a professor marking the practical complete and praising the player's control

hemomancy.circus.school.practical.about: asking to begin their practical examination

hemomancy.circus.school.preparation.about: a professor telling the player to attune a Marionette Crossbar and charge it at a Puppeteer's Spindle with spare Filaments, that a lesson shows only the ordeal recipe and the shape stays locked until the Cardinal Ordeal is beaten with its Degree, blood, frame and reusable Crossbar, and that a practical uses the player's own known bodies against two live rehearsal threats within twenty blocks and five minutes, retrying by recalling or walking off

hemomancy.circus.school.report.about: asking the Threadkeeper to review their apprenticeship and investigation

hemomancy.circus.school.report_complete.about: the Threadkeeper saying the player's completed work is entered in the account and the school recognizes the progress

hemomancy.circus.school.report_incomplet.about: the Threadkeeper saying there is still work to see and pointing the player to the Side section of their Assignment Ledger

hemomancy.circus.school.retry.about: a message that the practical is over, the player should return to the professor to retry, and their instruction and finished work stay on the record

hemomancy.circus.school.reward.about: a message that guest payment is settled and a count of Filaments (the number) is set aside for collection from a Threadkeeper

hemomancy.circus.school.reward.delivered.about: a message that guest payment is settled and a count of Filaments (the number) has been placed in the player's pack

hemomancy.circus.school.ring_blocked.about: a message that the practice space is blocked or wet and the player should clear it before returning for the exercise

hemomancy.circus.school.ringmaster.curri.about: the Ringmaster saying the Troupe is a school as well as a show, listing the Acrobat's pursuit, Dagger Thrower's focus, Stilt Walker's attention, Strongman's protection, Beast Tamer's rupture, Fire Breather's restraint and Retired Understudy's memory, and that a lesson readies you for the ordeal, winning the ordeal gives the shape, and trust is earned in a practical

hemomancy.circus.school.ringmaster.facul.about: the Ringmaster saying the Threadkeeper prepares the player's instrument while he teaches coordination in the final act as it has always run, that the player may finish every lesson and refuse his offer or step into his act without every professor's approval, that the Brined Court is only a neighbor, and the Crossbar's strings are not theirs to give

hemomancy.circus.school.status.degree.about: a professor saying the player has not reached the Degree their shape needs yet, and inviting them to study how it is built and the Troupe's history meanwhile

hemomancy.circus.school.status.lesson.about: a professor saying the player is ready for personal instruction and offering to teach the shape

hemomancy.circus.school.status.mastered.about: a professor saying the player has passed the practical and may rerun the exercise once per Minecraft day as a paid guest act

hemomancy.circus.school.status.ordeal.about: a professor saying instruction is on record and the player must now prepare the frame and beat the shape's Cardinal Ordeal

hemomancy.circus.school.status.practical.about: a professor saying the player knows the shape and should call it on their own Crossbar and show its purpose in the rehearsal ring

hemomancy.circus.school.status.preparati.about: the Threadkeeper explaining that Crossbars, Filaments, inspections and reports all go through the Threadhouse while the final act belongs to the Ringmaster

hemomancy.circus.school.take_lesson.about: asking a professor to teach them their puppet shape

hemomancy.circus.school.target.about: a short name label for the practice dummy

hemomancy.circus.school.testimony.about: asking about the wrong audience and the missing understudy

hemomancy.circus.school.unlock_first.about: a message that the shape must be unlocked through its Cardinal Ordeal first, and that a guest act also needs a passed practical and an available daily payment

hemomancy.dialogue.circus_acrobat.line1.about: the Acrobat boasting that by the time anyone works out where they landed, they have already left

hemomancy.dialogue.circus_acrobat.line2.about: the Acrobat joking that people say they vanish when really the player guessed the landing too early

hemomancy.dialogue.circus_acrobat.line3.about: the Acrobat explaining that the Mummer draws the eye away and they strike a moment after the player turns

hemomancy.dialogue.circus_fire_eater.lin.about: the Fire Breather explaining that swallowing fire really means teaching the body which burns to keep and which to breathe back out
the Fire Breather saying the torch is only a staff-form and the real work is making the breath carry farther
the Fire Breather admitting that without a watching crowd to hold the shape, they would only be burning their own throat

hemomancy.dialogue.circus_knife_thrower..about: the Dagger Thrower claiming the blade goes where it's thrown and it is the hand pointing out the landing that lies
the Dagger Thrower quipping that knives fly straight and it's the people who bend
the Dagger Thrower saying the first nine marks teach distance and the tenth teaches when to hold the knife

hemomancy.dialogue.circus_performer.leav.about: a player response ending the conversation with a performer

hemomancy.dialogue.circus_performer.welc.about: a performer telling the stranger to stand in place and let every eye find them, since strangers do better when the whole pavilion looks at one person

hemomancy.dialogue.circus_stilt_walker.l.about: the Stilt Walker saying that from up high they decide where the crowd looks for danger
the Stilt Walker explaining the stilts are braces and that to understand their walk the player should watch the cords, not the feet
the Stilt Walker saying that once every eye rises to meet them, somebody else owns the floor

hemomancy.dialogue.event.monolith_corner.about: narration of the Lodestone pressing a Monolithic Cornerstone into the player's hand, small, cold and far heavier than it should be
narration that the Lodestone has already given the player its cornerstone and will not give another
narration that the Lodestone stays silent because it answers only Archons who have worked a consecrated Armature

hemomancy.dialogue.monolith.option.accep.about: accepting the Monolith's cornerstone, written as a bracketed action

hemomancy.dialogue.monolith.option.ancho.about: asking the Monolith what the Armature still lacks

hemomancy.dialogue.monolith.option.ask_a.about: asking the Monolith to weigh the item they carry

hemomancy.dialogue.monolith.option.couns.about: asking the Monolith what it would have them do

hemomancy.dialogue.monolith.option.does_.about: asking the Monolith whether it knows them

hemomancy.dialogue.monolith.option.leave.about: leaving the Monolith, written as a bracketed action

hemomancy.dialogue.monolith.option.press.about: asking the Monolith to press further

hemomancy.dialogue.monolith.option.ripen.about: asking the Monolith what it means by ripening

hemomancy.dialogue.monolith.option.the_o.about: asking the Monolith what became of the others who stood before it

hemomancy.dialogue.monolith.option.what_.about: asking the Monolith what it is
asking the Monolith what it measures
asking the Monolith what happens when it opens
asking the Monolith what will remain of it

hemomancy.dialogue.monolith.option.where.about: asking the Monolith where the Lodge found the thing it holds

hemomancy.dialogue.monolith.option.who_s.about: asking the Monolith who stood here before them

hemomancy.dialogue.monolith.option.why_n.about: asking the Monolith why it speaks to them now

hemomancy.dialogue.rapport.circus_acroba.about: asking the Acrobat about their first fall
the Acrobat recalling a first fall off a barn roof, small, landing wrong, climbing back up, and still doing so
a short unlock teaser hinting at the Acrobat talking in falls, with the first one coming out after trading for a while
asking the Acrobat whether they ever go up without a net
the Acrobat recalling the one time they climbed without a net and caught the rope a hand from the ground
the Acrobat admitting they laughed for an hour and shook for two, and now the net goes up first every time
a short unlock teaser hinting at a fall the Acrobat does not joke about

hemomancy.dialogue.rapport.circus_beast_.about: asking the Beast Tamer which animal was their first
the Beast Tamer remembering a one-eyed dog that came only to them after a month of sitting still, where the empty cage idea began
a short unlock teaser hinting at the Beast Tamer talking about animals and about themselves once trust is earned
asking the Beast Tamer whether they ever lost an animal to the show
the Beast Tamer remembering a little peacock spider who danced better than any of them
the Beast Tamer saying too many eyes on her for too many nights cost the spider, and that animals tell you when enough is enough
a short unlock teaser hinting at an empty cage the Beast Tamer will not explain to strangers

hemomancy.dialogue.rapport.circus_fire_e.about: asking the Fire Breather how they learned to breathe fire
the Fire Breather explaining they learned slowly over a winter, one second of flame then three of breath, a whole season for one second
a short unlock teaser hinting at the Fire Breather counting everything, their own story too, if the player counts along
asking the Fire Breather whether they were ever badly burned
the Fire Breather admitting to one burn from four seconds when they meant three, and now counting aloud so the crowd hears
the Fire Breather reciting the count one, two, three, stop, and saying the rest is costume and crowd
a short unlock teaser hinting at one count the Fire Breather keeps to themselves

hemomancy.dialogue.rapport.circus_knife_.about: asking the Dagger Thrower who taught them to throw
the Dagger Thrower claiming to be self-taught, badly, and bantering that the Strongman says they throw like a sailor, while sailors are actually better
a short unlock teaser hinting at the Dagger Thrower arguing with anyone and, after trading, arguing about themselves
asking the Dagger Thrower whether they have ever missed
the Dagger Thrower admitting to one miss, because knives fly straight and the people bend, and that night they bent
the Dagger Thrower saying she forgave them, they did not forgive themselves, and they still argue over who is right
a short unlock teaser hinting at one throw the Dagger Thrower does not laugh about

hemomancy.dialogue.rapport.circus_ringma.about: asking the Ringmaster where he got the hat
the Ringmaster saying the player will get the hat the way he did, by learning every act and holding every eye and taking it off a head that cannot hold the ring
a short unlock teaser hinting at the Ringmaster selling a show while the man behind it costs more
asking the Ringmaster whether he thinks about the understudies on the carousel
the Ringmaster admitting he thinks of the understudies every show, that he put them there, and would do it again
the Ringmaster telling the player not to wait for his apology but to watch the carousel, count the captives, and then decide what he is
a short unlock teaser hinting at one subject the Ringmaster will not play to the crowd

hemomancy.dialogue.rapport.circus_stilt_.about: asking the Stilt Walker whether they could have stopped the carousel
the Stilt Walker saying they saw the carousel start from up high and came down too slowly
the Stilt Walker vowing to keep watching, refusing to call a dead captive a liberated student, and promising not to miss another
a short unlock teaser hinting at the Stilt Walker watching the carousel more closely than the crowd
asking the Stilt Walker what they see from up there
the Stilt Walker saying they see who is lost, hurt or about to be, and watch the small ones first
a short unlock teaser hinting at the Stilt Walker seeing a great deal and saying little of it

hemomancy.dialogue.rapport.circus_strong.about: asking the Strongman what strength is for
the Strongman answering that strength is for holding things up, mostly people
the Strongman turning the question back on the player, asking what their strength is for, since strong and good for nothing comes to nothing
a short unlock teaser hinting at the Strongman having a question for the player once he trusts them
asking the Strongman how they got so strong
the Strongman explaining he carried his father's anvil every day until it felt light
a short unlock teaser hinting at the Strongman not talking to people he does not know

hemomancy.dialogue.rapport.circus_thread.about: asking the Threadkeeper whether they owe anyone
the Threadkeeper admitting to one red entry near the front of the ledger, written the night they joined
the Threadkeeper saying a little goes against the entry every show, it will never close, and they pay anyway
a short unlock teaser hinting at one ledger entry the Threadkeeper will not read aloud
asking the Threadkeeper what they keep in that ledger
the Threadkeeper explaining the ledger tracks who owes, who is owed, and who has stopped paying attention, and that the third column gets checked twice
a short unlock teaser hinting at the Threadkeeper keeping accounts, with the player's still short

hemomancy.dialogue.rapport.circus_unders.about: asking the Retired Understudy about their best role
the Retired Understudy recalling a best role as second gravedigger for three seasons without a flubbed line, covering the lead's mistakes
a short unlock teaser hinting at the Understudy remembering every name on every bill, if asked nicely and often
asking the Retired Understudy whether they remember the missing performers
the Retired Understudy saying they remember each missing performer's name, cues, and the side of the stage they waited on
the Retired Understudy admitting they whisper the missing performers' names in the wings before each show so somebody gives them their call
a short unlock teaser hinting at a list of names the Understudy does not read to strangers

hemomancy.dialogue.rapport.monolith.the_.about: asking the Monolith what the player's blood tells it
the Monolith saying blood does not lie about its weight, the player's is heavier than last time, and that is all it says so far
a short unlock teaser hinting at tithing to the stone for a while so it may say what it reads in the player

hemomancy.dialogue.rapport.monolith.wher.about: asking the Monolith where the blood goes
a bracketed description of the stone being warmer where the player's blood went in, followed by the Monolith saying nothing given here stays here
the Monolith saying the blood goes down into a great deal of depth, where something has been told the player's name
a short unlock teaser hinting at giving the stone enough blood so it may say where the blood goes

hemomancy.monolith.already_breaking.about: narration that the stone has already begun to answer and the player should let it fall

hemomancy.monolith.archon.press_again.about: a bracketed description of the stone fever-hot and painful to touch, then the Monolith asking whether the player truly wants to press once more and break it open

hemomancy.monolith.armature_cornerstone..about: narration of the cornerstone cube separating from the Lodestone without breaking it, leaving a hollow that hums low and warm
the Monolith saying the rack has been taught to hold blood and ceremony by the Vicar but no one has taught it silence

the Monolith telling the player to take the small weight from it and offer it at a lit brazier in the Rite of the Monolithic Armature, so the consecrated frame will remember armor no voice should wear

hemomancy.monolith.counsel.bind_throne.about: the Monolith's counsel, telling the player to bind a Covenant Throne to their Fane and sit in it, because it wants the covenant to have a seat

hemomancy.monolith.counsel.chamber_retur.about: the Monolith's counsel, telling the player that their own rite opens the Chamber of Will using a Grand Threshold floor and an echo shard in the brazier, and that they must go in and come back out, since a guided visit does not count

hemomancy.monolith.counsel.complete_vigi.about: the Monolith's counsel, telling the player to summon a recruited Vicar to the Fane with their ancestral ledger, give them a rite station for the Covenant Vigil, and keep them there to the end, since an interrupted vigil earns nothing

hemomancy.monolith.counsel.found_bloodli.about: the Monolith's counsel, saying the stone reads no line in the player, and telling them to perform the Rite of Bloodline Founding at Lesser Communion with blaze powder in the brazier, because an unsigned ledger founds nothing

hemomancy.monolith.counsel.found_fane.about: the Monolith's counsel that the line is founded but the ground is not: perform the Rite of the Founding Fane at Grand Dominion with Sanguine Quintessence in the Focus, a Nautilus Shell in the brazier, and a Bloodwell and Stakes bound; if the line already has a Fane, stand inside it and project into its Bloodwell yourself

hemomancy.monolith.counsel.past_the_seed.about: the Monolith's counsel, saying the player already carried a Seed out of a stone like it, that it sets no more conditions, and that pressing further for another will not change what they are

hemomancy.monolith.counsel.perform_blood.about: the Monolith's counsel, saying the Line and Fane stand and one condition remains: the Rite of the Bloodline Covenant, which opens the sixth Degree

hemomancy.monolith.counsel.perform_hemat.about: the Monolith's counsel, saying the player came back, sat and kept the Vigil, that it felt each, and telling them to perform the Rite of the Hematic Order

hemomancy.monolith.counsel.press_further.about: the Monolith's counsel, saying it has no more conditions, that pressing further opens it, and that the Qliphoth Seed inside is not handed over but must be taken by the player

hemomancy.monolith.dormant.about: narration that the stone has nothing more to say

hemomancy.monolith.gate.elsewhere.about: a message that part of the player is elsewhere and the stone will not open for what is left

hemomancy.monolith.gate.hint.about: a hint that the eye has closed but not gone, and would look again for a little of the player's blood

hemomancy.monolith.gate.inside.about: a message that the player is already where the stone leads

hemomancy.monolith.gate.no_blood.about: a message that too little of the player remains to wake the stone

hemomancy.monolith.gate.refused.about: a message that the stone does not know the player's blood

hemomancy.monolith.guidance.archon.line1.about: the Monolith telling an Archon it has been waiting for them, that someone like them would not do, and that it had to be them

hemomancy.monolith.guidance.archon.line2.about: a bracketed description of the stone hot under the palm with something shifting its weight in a space too small for it, felt more than heard

hemomancy.monolith.guidance.illuminatus..about: a bracketed description of the stone faintly warm under the player's touch, which is new

the Monolith addressing an Illuminatus, saying the Lodge's gates stand open, the Vicar no longer walks ahead, the stone will counsel from here, the mycelial network under their feet whispers of dormant power, and the stone believes they are beginning to hear it

hemomancy.monolith.guidance.sanctified.l.about: a bracketed description of the stone warm and yielding under the palm like skin over muscle

the Monolith addressing a Sanctified of the Covenant, saying the Loom taught them to make memory on purpose and it would now have them enter the inward room, since their own rite opens the Chamber of Will where memory, scar and will become architecture

hemomancy.monolith.item_hint.about: the prompt inviting the player to bring an item close so the stone can weigh it, noting that it says little

hemomancy.monolith.item_inquiry.fragment.about: the Monolith saying a fragment is still warm with remembered pressure and quiet, though memory moves through it
the Monolith warning to use the fragment carefully because alone it teaches nothing and only resonates

hemomancy.monolith.item_inquiry.minecraf.about: the Monolith confirming the old world kept such relics and that this one resonates with thresholds, anchors and return paths
the Monolith advising that a familiar relic can still serve an uncommon rite and should be treated as unknown until its place is learned

hemomancy.monolith.item_inquiry.qliphoth.about: the Monolith saying Qliphoth reagents open a path where doctrine thins and, once the player stands on it, draw them forward
the Monolith telling the player to proceed only if they intend to finish the conversation

hemomancy.monolith.item_inquiry.rite_sit.about: the Monolith saying the item belongs to the high covenant sequence of foundation, offering, witness and consequence
the Monolith telling the player they are no longer assembling tools but assembling conditions

hemomancy.monolith.item_inquiry.saint.li.about: the Monolith saying Saint matter and Saint echoes suit the oldest rites because they have already outlasted one fall
the Monolith saying what the player carries proves continuity, not victory

hemomancy.monolith.lodestone_name.about: the display name of the Monolith's stone object, the Crimson Lodestone

hemomancy.monolith.lore.does_it_know_me..about: the Monolith saying it knows the player's weight and that it has changed since they first stood there
the Monolith saying it keeps every change and what it keeps, it reads

hemomancy.monolith.lore.ripening.line1.about: a bracketed description of the stone hot, damp and leaning toward the player's hand, then the Monolith saying the player knows the word ripening and has felt it under the skin

hemomancy.monolith.lore.ripening.line2.about: the Monolith saying the Degrees were a calendar, it only kept the count, and asking whether no one told the player

hemomancy.monolith.lore.the_others.line1.about: the Monolith saying some climbed past it and some stopped there and stayed stopped

hemomancy.monolith.lore.the_others.line2.about: the Monolith saying it kept the weight of each but the weight does not say where they went

hemomancy.monolith.lore.what_it_measures.about: the Monolith saying it reads what the work leaves in the blood, which the Lodge called a record
the Monolith saying the record is accurate but the Lodge never asked who reads it

hemomancy.monolith.lore.what_opens.line1.about: the Monolith saying that when it opens it stops being a stone and what it holds stops being held

hemomancy.monolith.lore.what_opens.line2.about: the Monolith saying the player will walk to what it holds and take it themselves, may turn back, and asking whether they will

hemomancy.monolith.lore.what_remains.lin.about: the Monolith saying a split, quiet husk will remain that keeps the shape of the door
the Monolith saying the husk will know the player's blood and, if fed, will look again

hemomancy.monolith.lore.where_found.line.about: a bracketed description of the stone yielding warm as a forearm, then the Monolith saying what it holds was found deep under old rock as a red vein in the Second Age
the Monolith saying the Lodge cut the thing free and closed the stone around it, kept careful notes, and did not keep it asleep

hemomancy.monolith.lore.who_stood_here.l.about: a bracketed description of the warmth under the player's hand not changing, then the Monolith saying those who came this far are kept as weight, not faces
the Monolith saying few came back a second time and each stood where the player stands

hemomancy.monolith.lore.why_now.line1.about: the Monolith saying the Vicar has stepped back and no one stands above the player at the outpost now

hemomancy.monolith.lore.why_now.line2.about: the Monolith saying the stone takes the Vicar's place and has waited for this Degree

hemomancy.monolith.overgrown.about: narration that something takes root in the stone's cracks and will not be giving it back

hemomancy.monolith.unworthy.about: narration that the monolith is silent, cold and hard under the player's hand because they have not yet proven themselves worthy

hemomancy.monolith.what_are_you.archon.about: the Monolith telling a close Archon it can speak plainly: what is inside it knows what is inside them, they are the same thing, and asking if they feel it ripening

hemomancy.monolith.what_are_you.illumina.about: the Monolith describing itself as a lodestone of the Order built by the Crimson Lodge in the Second Age to measure, which it does, remembering every Harbinger who stood before it, every degree and every name, while also watching what it measures

hemomancy.monolith.what_are_you.sanctifi.about: the Monolith admitting it contains something, sealed in the stone by the Lodge in the Second Age, which they called measurement

hemomancy.trade.circus_acrobat.rigging_l.about: a trade card line from the Acrobat offering eight String for rigging line, saying rigging comes first and it's for when the player falls
a short title for the trade card about rigging line

hemomancy.trade.circus_acrobat.thanks.about: the Acrobat thanking the player after a trade and wishing them a soft landing

hemomancy.trade.circus_beast_tamer.feed..about: a trade card line from the Beast Tamer saying goats eat first and that eight wheat buys a name tag for an animal the player means to keep
a short title for the trade card about feed

hemomancy.trade.circus_beast_tamer.thank.about: the Beast Tamer thanking the player and saying the animals will eat well tonight

hemomancy.trade.circus_fire_eater.fuel.l.about: a trade card line from the Fire Breather asking four blaze powder counted out, giving a draught back so the fire waits its turn

hemomancy.trade.circus_fire_eater.fuel.t.about: a short title for the trade card about fuel

hemomancy.trade.circus_fire_eater.thanks.about: the Fire Breather thanking the player after counting all four items

hemomancy.trade.circus_knife_thrower.app.about: the Dagger Thrower rejecting a trade item as a bent stick, not a blade, which even they won't throw

hemomancy.trade.circus_knife_thrower.tha.about: the Dagger Thrower, after repairing a blade, saying it's as straight as a knife, which is to say mostly
the Dagger Thrower grudgingly admiring the edge of a fine blade and admitting the player keeps a good one

hemomancy.trade.circus_knife_thrower.wor.about: a trade card line from the Dagger Thrower accepting any worn sword and insisting it's balanced better than new, though nobody agrees
a short title for the trade card about worn blades

hemomancy.trade.circus_ringmaster.bell.l.about: a trade card line from the Ringmaster asking for a bell from a player of the fourth Degree, paying four Filaments to string the act

hemomancy.trade.circus_ringmaster.bell.t.about: a short title for the trade card about a bell for the act

hemomancy.trade.circus_ringmaster.curios.about: a trade card line from the Ringmaster asking for something strange like a relic, trophy or wreck salvage, saying rarer means a louder crowd
a short title for the trade card about a curiosity

hemomancy.trade.circus_ringmaster.ring_p.about: a trade card line from the Ringmaster asking for sixteen planks because the ring takes a beating every night and must be fed
a short title for the trade card about planks for the ring

hemomancy.trade.circus_ringmaster.specta.about: a trade card line from the Ringmaster offering payment for holding a performance to its end without looking away or leaving
a short title for the trade card about a spectacle

hemomancy.trade.circus_ringmaster.thanks.about: the Ringmaster thanking the player after a trade, saying he hears the crowd, or soon will
the Ringmaster praising a rare, strange trade item as a proper act that is now his

hemomancy.trade.circus_stilt_walker.stic.about: a trade card line from the Stilt Walker asking sixteen sticks to make new legs because theirs are wearing short, giving scaffolding in return, and telling the player to climb slowly
a short title for the trade card about sticks

hemomancy.trade.circus_stilt_walker.than.about: the Stilt Walker thanking the player and telling them to mind their footing when high up

hemomancy.trade.circus_strongman.iron_ba.about: a trade card line from the Strongman asking four iron for his bar and calling the return strength in a bottle to spend on somebody
a short title for the trade card about iron for the bar

hemomancy.trade.circus_strongman.thanks.about: the Strongman thanking the player and telling them to carry something that isn't theirs

hemomancy.trade.circus_threadkeeper.ledg.about: a trade card line from the Threadkeeper asking six sheets of paper entered against two Enthralling Filaments, saying the account balances
a short title for the trade card about paper for the ledger

hemomancy.trade.circus_threadkeeper.than.about: the Threadkeeper confirming the trade is entered and nothing is owed either way

hemomancy.trade.circus_understudy.prompt.about: a trade card line from the Retired Understudy asking three books for the prompt corner where somebody keeps the names, offering a mask and a warning to mind the flubs
a short title for the trade card about books for the prompt corner

hemomancy.trade.circus_understudy.thanks.about: the Retired Understudy thanking the player and promising their name goes in the prompt book

hemomancy.trade.monolith.deep.line.about: a trade card line from the Monolith naming a 1,000 mL measure from the sixth Degree that gives two poultices as the weight goes down

hemomancy.trade.monolith.deep.title.about: a short title for the trade card about the deep measure

hemomancy.trade.monolith.measure.line.about: a trade card line from the Monolith naming a measure where the player puts a palm to the stone, gives 500 mL, and receives two salves

hemomancy.trade.monolith.measure.title.about: a short title for the trade card about a measure

hemomancy.trade.monolith.thanks.about: the Monolith noting the trade and saying the weight is kept

hemomancy.trade.monolith.weight.line.about: a trade card line from the Monolith naming a heavier measure of 750 mL against the stone, returning one warm poultice

hemomancy.trade.monolith.weight.title.about: a short title for the trade card about a heavier measure

message.hemomancy.circus.route.chosen.li.about: a system message that the player is bound to Liberation, must sever the captives' threads and break the carousel's anchors, and can change their mind once

message.hemomancy.circus.route.chosen.su.about: a system message that the player is bound to Succession, must learn every act and then come for the Ringmaster's hat, and can change their mind once

message.hemomancy.circus_ringmaster_enti.about: a system message that Thread Ripper remains in the creature's memory and should be kept until it can be absorbed at a lit Iron Brazier
